sources.title: David Tong, Electromagnetism, University of Cambridge Part II Mathematical Tripos lecture notes (2026 author-hosted revision, 236 pp.)
sources.locator: \u00a74.3.3 printed pp. 89-90 (reflection off a conductor); \u00a77.4 'Reflection and Refraction' printed pp. 185-188; \u00a77.4.1 'Fresnel Equations' printed pp. 189-191; \u00a77.4.2 'Total Internal Reflection' printed pp. 191-193; \u00a77.6.2 'Electromagnetic Waves in Conductors' printed pp. 207-209 (PDF pagination offset +8, 236 pp.). The intervening \u00a77.5 'Dispersion' and \u00a77.6.1 'The Drude Model' passages were not read and no scaffolded claim rests on them; the sections above were inspected in the fetched 2026 author-hosted revision (1 882 418 bytes, 236 pages) including the displayed derivations, interface algebra, root selection and skin-depth formulas.

contents.name: \u00a74.3.3 pp. 89-90, normal incidence on an ideal conductor: E=0 inside, the reflected wave Eref=-E0 y hat e^{i(-kx-\u03c9t)} giving vanishing tangential E on the surface, and the surface current K=2E0/(c\u03bc0) y hat e^{-i\u03c9t} from the tangential-H jump
contents.reason: The approved wave-interface proofs provide dielectric phase matching/Fresnel formulas and finite constant-Ohmic skin depth. The guide/cavity pair declares PEC trace/current geometry and its spectral solutions; it does not promise this additional explicit flat-conductor reflection/surface-current calculation. That source-specific application is outside the approved inventory; all PEC geometry, guide/cavity completeness and existing reflection claims remain intact.

contents.name: \u00a74.3.3 pp. 89-90, oblique reflection off a conductor: the two electric continuity conditions, \u03c9'=\u03c9 and polarization preservation, the reflected wavevector k'=-k cos\u03b8 x hat + k sin\u03b8 z hat and the law 'angle of incidence equals angle of reflection'
contents.reason: The approved wave-interface proofs provide dielectric phase matching/Fresnel formulas and finite constant-Ohmic skin depth. The guide/cavity pair declares PEC trace/current geometry and its spectral solutions; it does not promise this additional explicit flat-conductor reflection/surface-current calculation. That source-specific application is outside the approved inventory; all PEC geometry, guide/cavity completeness and existing reflection claims remain intact.

contents.name: \u00a77.4 pp. 185-188, the two-dielectric interface: incident, reflected and transmitted plane waves with independently varying amplitudes, frequencies and wavevectors, and the four matching conditions (7.17)-(7.20) with no surface charge or current; equality of the phase factors for all time forces common frequency and equality of the tangential wavevector components (7.22)-(7.24)
contents.support: The scaffolded theorem is exactly this reduction: from the two tangential interface identities and the non-degenerate plane-wave data it derives common tangential wavevector and frequency by the character-independence lemma [[lem-em-exponential-character-open-set-independence]], and records that the normal identities are part of the model but unused.

contents.name: \u00a77.4 pp. 187-188, the dispersion relations \u03c9I=v1 kI, \u03c9R=v1 kR, \u03c9T=v2 kT give the law of reflection \u03b8I=\u03b8R and Snell's law sin\u03b8I/v1 = sin\u03b8T/v2, i.e. n1 sin\u03b8I = n2 sin\u03b8T (7.25)
contents.support: Clause (c) of the scaffolded theorem derives this in the real-propagation case from the common tangential wavevector and the dispersion relation k\u00b7k=\u03b5\u03bc\u03c9\u00b2 of the medium plane-wave supplier.

contents.name: \u00a77.4.1 pp. 189-190, normal/s-polarized Fresnel equations (7.26): ER/EI=(n1 cos\u03b8I - n2 cos\u03b8T)/(n1 cos\u03b8I + n2 cos\u03b8T), ET/EI=2n1 cos\u03b8I/(n1 cos\u03b8I + n2 cos\u03b8T), including the \u03b8=0 normal-incidence reduction
contents.support: The scaffolded oblique theorem contains these formulas in the fixed tangential-electric convention with the TE admittance Y^s=kz/(\u03bc\u03c9); the normal-incidence specialization is [[pthm-em-normal-fresnel]](c).

contents.name: \u00a77.4.1 pp. 190-191, parallel/p-polarized Fresnel equations (7.27) and Brewster's angle: r_p=0 when n1 cos\u03b8T = n2 cos\u03b8I, equivalently \u03b8I+\u03b8T=\u03c0/2 and tan\u03b8B=n2/n1 (\u224856\u00b0 for air to glass); only the normal polarization is reflected at \u03b8B
contents.support: The scaffolded example instantiates this with n1=1, n2=3/2, giving tan\u03b8B=3/2, \u03b8B+\u03b8t=\u03c0/2, r_p=0 and the surviving s-reflection r_s=-5/13 with R_s+T_s=1 exactly.

contents.name: \u00a77.4.2 pp. 191-193, total internal reflection: \u03b8C with sin\u03b8C=n2/n1, the imaginary normal component kT\u00b7x hat= \u00b1 i\u03c9\u03b1/v2 beyond \u03b8C, the choice of the decaying sign and the evanescent transmitted wave
contents.support: Clauses (d) and (e) of the scaffolded theorem give the evanescent selection k_t= \u03ba+i\u03b2n, |r_s|=|r_p|=1, the vanishing normal averaged flux and the decay; the explicit numbers are checked in [[ex-em-evanescent-flux-example]].

contents.name: \u00a77.6.2 pp. 207-209, waves in conductors: the Ohm's law ansatz J=\u03c3(\u03c9)E with its wavelength/mean-free-path caveat, the effective permittivity \u03b5eff=\u03b5+i\u03c3/\u03c9, the transverse conclusion and the dispersion relation (7.54) k\u00b7k=\u03bc\u03b5eff(\u03c9)\u03c9\u00b2
contents.support: Clauses (a)-(b) of the scaffolded theorem derive the complex propagation constant from the medium plane-wave amplitude conditions with the Ohmic current and give the exact closed-form attenuation constant.

contents.name: \u00a77.6.2 pp. 208-209, low-frequency regime: k=(1+i)\u221a(\u03bc\u03c9\u03c3DC/2), skin depth \u03b4=\u221a(2/(\u03bc\u03c9\u03c3DC)), the \u03c0/4 phase relation and the \u03c3=0 no-attenuation limit
contents.support: The scaffolded theorem states the exact \u03b4 and the explicit bounded good-conductor bounds |q-\u221a(b/2)|\u22642t\u221a(b/2), |\u03b4-\u221a(2/b)|\u22644t\u221a(2/b) for t=\u03b5\u03c9/\u03c3\u22641/4, the poor-conductor counterpart and the \u03c3=0 exclusion \u03b4=+\u221e; the quadrature coefficient q/p is recorded exactly.

contents.name: \u00a77.6.2 pp. 208-209, high-frequency/plasma-frequency regime: \u03b5eff\u2248\u03b5\u2080(1-\u03c9p\u00b2/\u03c9\u00b2), transparent propagation for \u03c9>\u03c9p, total reflection for \u03c9<\u03c9p, and the mean-free-path condition for using Ohm's law in a varying field
contents.reason: The approved material branch uses an explicitly adopted general causal response kernel and proved dispersion under its stated analytic/subtraction hypotheses; the approved conductor branch has constant scalar Ohmic conductivity. Microscopic oscillator/Drude/plasma-frequency specializations in this source row are not promised by either branch and have no supplied destination. Both general dispersion and constant-Ohmic claims remain intact.

sources.title: David J. Griffiths, Introduction to Electrodynamics, 3rd edition (Prentice Hall, 1999, 596-page retained scan)
sources.locator: \u00a79.3.1 printed pp. 382-383; \u00a79.3.2 printed pp. 384-386 with Problems 9.13-9.14 on p. 386; \u00a79.3.3 printed pp. 386-392 with Problems 9.15-9.16 on p. 392; \u00a79.4.1 printed pp. 392-396 with Problems 9.18-9.20 on pp. 395-396; \u00a79.4.2 printed pp. 396-398 with Problem 9.21 on p. 398; Problem 9.37 printed pp. 413-414. Retained 596-page third-edition scan (13 484 424 bytes) with OCR noise in the text layer; the displayed formulas cited below were cross-checked against Tong and against the local computations in the batch notes. The intervening \u00a79.4.3 expository text on the frequency dependence of permittivity (pp. 398-413) was not read and no claim rests on it; pagination of the scan is the printed pagination.

contents.name: \u00a79.3.1 pp. 382-383, Maxwell in a linear homogeneous medium (9.65)-(9.67), the speed v=1/\u221a(\u03b5\u03bc) and index n (9.68)-(9.70), the energy density (9.71), Poynting vector (9.72) and intensity (9.73), with the transcription 'all previous results carry over'
contents.support: The scaffolded medium plane-wave theorem supplies the amplitude conditions, dispersion, transverse structure and the period-averaged energy density and flux in exactly this transcription, with the stored-energy model of [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]] fixing u and S.

contents.name: \u00a79.3.2 pp. 384-386, normal-incidence boundary conditions (9.74), the amplitude system (9.78)-(9.82), the reflection and transmission coefficients (9.86)-(9.88) with R+T=1
contents.support: Clause (c) of the scaffolded theorem reproduces the amplitude system with the admittances 1/Z_j, the amplitude formulas and the flux budget R+T=1 with R=r\u00b2 and T=(Z1/Z2)t\u00b2.

contents.name: \u00a79.3.2 Problems 9.13-9.14 p. 386, exact reflection and transmission coefficients without \u03bc1=\u03bc2=\u03bc0, and the proof that the reflected and transmitted polarizations must lie along the incident one
contents.support: The scaffolded theorem keeps the general Z_j (arbitrary positive \u03b5_j,\u03bc_j) and derives polarization preservation from the two vector interface equations; the flux budget is stated without the \u03bc1=\u03bc2 assumption.

contents.name: \u00a79.3.3 pp. 386-388, the exponential-factor matching argument (9.93)-(9.95): the boundary conditions must hold for all x, y and t, so kI\u00b7r=kR\u00b7r=kT\u00b7r on the interface and the components are separately equal (9.96)-(9.98), giving the plane of incidence, \u03b8I=\u03b8R (9.99) and Snell's law (9.100)
contents.support: The scaffolded theorem proves the same conclusion under explicit non-degeneracy hypotheses by the open-set character-independence lemma, which supplies the rigorous form of 'otherwise a slight change in x would destroy the equality'.

contents.name: \u00a79.3.3 Problem 9.15 p. 392, the exponential identity A e^{iax}+B e^{ibx}=C e^{icx} for all x implies a=b=c and A+B=C
contents.support: This one-variable exponential-identity argument is the n=1 base case of the character-independence lemma [[lem-em-exponential-character-open-set-independence]] used by the scaffolded phase-matching proof, so it is absorbed there rather than built as a separate item.

contents.name: \u00a79.3.3 pp. 389-391, boundary system (9.101) and Fresnel's equations (9.105)-(9.109) for polarization in the plane of incidence
contents.support: Clause (a) of the scaffolded theorem gives the same system in the fixed tangential-electric convention with the TM admittance Y^p=\u03b5\u03c9/kz and the solution formulas of [[lem-em-admittance-interface-solve]].

contents.name: \u00a79.3.3 pp. 390-392, Brewster's angle (9.111)-(9.112) tan\u03b8B=n2/n1 for \u03bc1=\u03bc2, and the intensity coefficients (9.113)-(9.116) with R+T=1 for the parallel polarization
contents.support: Clause (c) of the scaffolded theorem states the general criterion r_p=0 \u21d4 Y^p_1=Y^p_2 and the equal-permeability consequence tan\u03b8B=n2/n1 with uniqueness; clause (b) gives R_\u03c7+T_\u03c7=1. The explicit instance is [[ex-em-brewster-angle-example]].

contents.name: \u00a79.3.3 Problem 9.16 p. 392, perpendicular-polarization Fresnel equations, absence of a Brewster angle, normal-incidence reduction, and reflection/transmission coefficients adding to 1
contents.support: The scaffolded theorem treats the TE polarization in the same clause (a)-(b) structure, and [[ex-em-brewster-angle-example]] records that the s-reflection does not vanish at \u03b8B for n1\u2260n2.

contents.name: \u00a79.4.1 pp. 392-395, conduction: Ohm's law (9.117), free-charge relaxation (9.119)-(9.120), the modified wave equations (9.122), the complex wave number (9.124) k\u00b2=\u03bc\u03b5\u03c9\u00b2+i\u03bc\u03c3\u03c9, its decomposition (9.125) k=k+i\u03ba and the skin depth d=1/\u03ba (9.128)
contents.support: The scaffolded theorem derives k\u00b2=\u03b5\u03bc\u03c9\u00b2+i\u03bc\u03c3\u03c9 from the Ohmic amplitude conditions, selects the decaying root p+iq and gives the exact \u03b4=1/q with the closed form \u221a(2(r+a))/b.

contents.name: \u00a79.4.1 pp. 394-396 and Problems 9.18-9.20 pp. 395-396, transverse fields, the magnetic amplitude relation (9.131), the phase lag (9.135)-(9.136), the good- and poor-conductor skin-depth exercises (9.19) and the energy-density/intensity exercises (9.20)
contents.support: The scaffolded theorem records the transverse structure and the exact quadrature coefficient q/p= \u221a(1+t\u00b2)-t, the good- and poor-conductor bounded remainder inequalities and the exact decay; the numeric instances of Problems 9.18-9.20 are disposed separately below.

contents.name: Problems 9.18, 9.19(b),(c) and 9.20 pp. 395-396, numerical exercises with measured material data (silver coating thickness at 10\u00b9\u2070 Hz, metal skin depth in the visible, pure-water skin depth, magnetic-to-electric energy ratio)
contents.reason: These are exercises with real-material conductivities and frequencies; this pair reports no measured datum, and the declared-parameter illustration in [[ex-em-skin-depth-approximation-example]] deliberately uses declared, non-measured parameters instead of importing empirical values.

contents.name: \u00a79.4.2 pp. 396-398, reflection at a conducting surface: boundary conditions (9.139), the complex \u03b2=k2/(\u03bc2\u03c9)\u00b7\u03bc1v1, the amplitude ratio (9.147), and the perfect-conductor limit (9.148) with total reflection
contents.support: Clause (d) of the scaffolded theorem covers exactly the finite-\u03c3 conducting half-space: Y2=\u03ba2(\u03c9)/(\u03bc2\u03c9) complex, the amplitude formulas and the flux budget |r|\u00b2+(ReY2/Y1)|t|\u00b2=1 with the absorbed fraction; the \u03c3=\u221e limit is excluded by its scope clause.

contents.name: Problem 9.21 p. 398, the numerical reflection coefficient at an air-to-silver interface at optical frequencies
contents.reason: A numerical exercise with a measured silver conductivity and an optical frequency; no measured value is adopted on this pair, and the finite-Ohmic reflection formula itself is already scaffolded in [[pthm-em-normal-fresnel]](d) without the numerical instance.

contents.name: Problem 9.37 pp. 413-414, total internal reflection and the evanescent wave: E_T=E_{0T}e^{-Kz}e^{i(kx-\u03c9t)} with k=(\u03c9/c)n1 sin\u03b8I and K=(\u03c9/c)\u221a(n1\u00b2sin\u00b2\u03b8I-n2\u00b2), |r|=1 for both polarizations, and no average energy transported into medium 2
contents.support: Clause (d) of the scaffolded theorem states the evanescent selection, |r_s|=|r_p|=1, the decay and the vanishing normal averaged flux; [[ex-em-evanescent-flux-example]] computes the explicit instance with sin\u03b8I=4/5 and records the surviving tangential flux.
